summary:
Qumulo is a software-defined cloud data platform. Our core is a distributed storage operating system in C & Rust, holding exabytes in the datacenter, at the edge, and natively in the cloud. Qumulo serves everything from a hospital's medical imaging archive to an animation studio's render farm in an environment where 99% correct doesn't cut it.
About the Role:
Joining us for our Summer 2027 internship program, you'd learn and work across our distributed storage engine and the services that help customers store, manage, and protect their data, under the guidance of experienced senior engineers.
This includes a fault-tolerant block layer that erasure-codes and distributes data beneath the file system, a transactional file system where aggregates roll up as they change so a query across billions of files answers in real time instead of walking a tree, and that same machinery drives quotas, capacity trends, snapshot policy, multiple access protocols, plus replication and backup - all running in userspace.
All of which makes Qumulo a distributed operating system problem: scheduling, memory hierarchy, protection, and concurrency. We're AI-forward and specific about what that means. You will learn to use agents to help write code while developing your engineering judgment to ensure every design decision is correct, because nothing ships that isn't right.
Why intern at Qumulo:
Qumulo blends the flexibility of a startup with the security of a mature and profitable organization. Here you'll work closely with a small team of smart, capable engineers who will serve as your mentors. Opinions are expected, disagreement is normal, and you'll get hands-on experience taking projects from ideation to release. We value quality, correctness, and performance. Our architecture, protocols, and patents are public, so you can read how most of this works before you talk to us - and we're small enough that the work you do during your internship will actually show up in the product.

summary:
ABOUT OVERVIEW ENERGY
Overview Energy is a mission-driven team committed to building a new layer of energy infrastructure: satellites in geosynchronous orbit that redirect solar energy to terrestrial solar projects via passively safe near-infrared light. We're in the earliest phase, where the ground beacon our satellites will point to is aligned, characterized, and field-corrected end-to-end by a small, dedicated team. Headquartered in the Northern Virginia / Washington, DC area and backed by world-class investors, we are advancing the next generation of clean energy technology.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We're looking for an Optics Intern to help with the design and building of our ground beacon from the optical bench to a field test site. The beacon is the pointing reference the satellite system will depend on. If it isn't aligned and characterized correctly, nothing downstream works.
You'll work hands-on with the emitter and the observational telescope: aligning the laser, characterizing its output, and co-aligning the beacon with the telescope. Then you'll own a problem we haven't solved yet. Once the system is transported to the test site, alignment may shift. You'll design the procedure that brings it back.
This internship supports our program under a Department of War (DoW) energy investment program. You'll work alongside our optics and hardware engineers, and your alignment data will feed directly into hardware decisions we make.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Align the beacon laser within its emitter and verify pointing outside the emitter aperture
- Characterize laser output - power, beam profile, divergence, and pointing stability - and document the results
- Co-align the beacon laser with the observational telescope and verify boresight
- Design a repeatable field alignment procedure that corrects misalignment introduced during transport and installation at the DoW site
- Write that procedure so a non-optics operator can execute it, then validate it hands-on before delivery
